title: Great for Basics, But Needs More Desktop Features
body:
Google Sheets is a reliable app for viewing and making basic edits on the go. It’s smooth, syncs well across devices, and works great for quick tasks. However, it lacks many of the advanced features available on desktop, which limits its usefulness for serious work.

For starters, mobile users should be able to create personal filter views even in view-only files—just like on desktop. Pivot tables and conditional formatting are also essential tools that are either missing or too limited in the mobile version. Navigating and linking cell references across multiple sheets is clunky, and editing data validation rules or dropdowns is barely supported.

If Google could bring at least 80% of the desktop functionality to mobile, this app would be a powerhouse. Until then, it’s best for light edits and quick checks—not full-scale data work.

title: Not the best spreadsheet app for iOS or iPadOS considering we are in 2022
body:
The app itself is good and can be used to accomplish basic tasks BUT the problem arises because the app is,

1) Heavily Underpowered- When compared to the web version the app version is heavily underpowered and can be very limiting to productivity and it lacks in the following domains but it is so underpowered compared to the web version that this list can go on and on but here is the summary:

a) NO conditional formatting- There is no option for conditional formatting none whatsoever, but if you have applied conditional formatting using the web version the conditional formatting will work in the app, google should bring conditional formatting to the app version considering conditional formatting is present in an app like numbers which is barely used by anyone why it should not be in a much used app like sheets.

b) NO paste special option- Unlike the web version which has the paste special option, there is no such option in the app, paste special option helps in pasting the value in the cell or column without pasting their formula or formatting, due to lack of paste special the formula along the values are pasted which defeats the purpose in most cases and is very very annoying, the irony is that this issue is reported on Google Help as early as 2019, 3 years down the line there is no paste special option to this date, there are work arounds but they are very exhaustive and reduce the productivity factor as a whole.

c) Good luck with functions- If you are a person who uses functions a lot like IF, AND, OR functions or any other function, Good Luck to you because if you type the syntax perfectly its all good, but if your syntax is wrong, trying to find the mistake(s) is like finding a needle in the haystack, where as in web version you can just highlight the parts of the function to check wether they are giving a true value, false value, responding or NOT responding at all.

2) You cannot use Web version of sheets in iPad- You can actually but it will be very slow and exhaustive, scrolling and entering values everything is slow, if you think that I will use the app for most of the time using the web version only to use conditional formatting or other options when it is absolutely necessary- Okay good luck with that because once you go to the sheets website, Safari will automatically open the app and there is no way to avoid it except to open sheets in an incognito tab which will NOT open the app and will let you stay in the web version but it has its own set of problems.

Conclusion- We are living in 2022 where line between iPads and Macs is growing thinner and thinner so if some functionality is available on desktop or notebook version of Safari should be also available in iOS version of safari but for some reason the web version in iOS is very slow, also the app should be on par with the web version but who knows they might just keep the app version watered down so that they can hog more data when you use the web version as iOS doesnot allow these practices.

The Sheets app is ranked 10 in productivity apps and I think Google/Alphabet should do justice to it.
